as_told.title: Kordylewski cloud as the source of 1920s long-delay radio echoes
as_told.place_text: L5 Lagrangian point between the Earth and the Moon

plain: The writer Robert Temple, in his book A New Science of Heaven, believes that Kordylewski clouds, which are clouds of plasma sitting at Lagrangian points (spots in space where gravitational pulls balance out), may explain the "long delay echoes" of the early 1920s, radio transmissions that seemed to come back long after they were sent. Michels lays out Temple's idea himself on two episodes. Once he puts the clouds between the Earth and the Sun, and once at a point between the Earth and the Moon. If Temple is right, a radio puzzle from a century ago would come from these clouds.
